rationale: B wins because it is more disciplined: four real lanes, fewer padded trend costumes, and sharper proof gates before anyone wastes a reporter's time. A's weakest tell is "When a business-only fintech decides it's ready to be a full-service bank"; Mercury has no charter and checking-plus-savings is not full-service banking. B still has one overcaffeinated line in "What the SVB windfall became," but it immediately asks for the missing SVB customer split instead of pretending the number proves itself.
gaps_in_A: "mass-market consumer bank" overstates an invite-only waitlist for checking and savings, and it muddies the partner-bank structure.
"well-capitalized, previously B2B-only player" invents capitalization that the update does not provide; profitability is not the same fact.
"A profitable business bank is wading into the notoriously thin margins of consumer banking" imports a market-margin thesis not supplied by the update and leans on generic fintech wisdom.
"When a business-only fintech decides it's ready to be a full-service bank" is padded category framing; without other examples, it is an n-of-1 trend wearing a fake mustache.
gaps_in_B: "What the SVB windfall became" overclaims benefit from SVB; the update says Mercury became well known after the collapse, not that it captured a windfall.
"business-only bank" is sloppy shorthand for a fintech using partner banks, and the distinction matters for this story.
"the first invites are where the distribution question gets answered" assumes waitlist sequencing that is not in the update.
"who is now squeezed from a new direction" is a little too certain before pricing, features, or target segment are disclosed.
